metadata.description: Scenario-Based Study Companion for AZ-500 certification - validates expertise in implementing security controls, maintaining security posture, managing identity and access, and protecting data, applications, and networks in Azure.

questions.title: Conditional Access Attack Scenarios
questions.scenario: Your organization experienced a credential stuffing attack where compromised credentials from another breach were used. Attackers logged in from unusual locations but passed MFA using push notification fatigue.
questions.questionText: Which Conditional Access configurations would have prevented this attack?

choices.text: Require MFA for all users without additional controls
Require number matching for MFA and block legacy authentication

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: What specific weakness in push-notification MFA did the attackers exploit, and which controls close that gap?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Number matching requires users to enter a number displayed on the sign-in screen into the Authenticator app, preventing blind approval of push notifications. Blocking legacy authentication prevents protocols that don't support MFA. Together, these stop credential stuffing with MFA fatigue.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• MFA fatigue: attackers spam push notifications hoping users approve accidentally.
  • Number matching and additional context (location, app) are now defaults in Entra ID.
  • Passwordless authentication (FIDO2, Windows Hello) eliminates password-based attacks entirely.
  • Sign-in risk policies can block when unusual behavior is detected.

questions.title: Privileged Identity Management
questions.scenario: Your security team identified that 50 users have permanent Global Administrator access. You need to reduce standing privileges while ensuring admins can still perform their duties when needed.
questions.questionText: How should you implement just-in-time access for privileged roles?

choices.text: Use shared admin accounts with MFA
Remove all admin access and grant on request via ticket
Create separate admin accounts with permanent access
Azure AD PIM with eligible assignments, approval workflows, and activation alerts

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which Azure service converts permanent role assignments into on-demand, time-limited activations?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure AD Privileged Identity Management (PIM) converts permanent assignments to eligible assignments. Users activate roles when needed, optionally requiring approval, MFA, and justification. Activations are time-limited (e.g., 8 hours) and fully audited. This dramatically reduces attack surface.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• PIM covers both Entra ID roles and Azure RBAC roles.
  • Configure maximum activation duration (1-24 hours typically).
  • Access reviews ensure ongoing role necessity.
  • Alert on suspicious activation patterns (after hours, unusual frequency).

questions.title: Identity Protection Policies
questions.scenario: You need to automatically respond to risky sign-ins and users with compromised credentials detected by Microsoft threat intelligence.
questions.questionText: Which Identity Protection policies should you configure?

choices.text: Require MFA for all sign-ins without risk assessment
Block all sign-ins from outside the country
Sign-in risk policy requiring MFA for medium/high risk, user risk policy requiring password change

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about which approach can automatically differentiate between sign-in risk and user risk, then apply separate remediation actions.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Configure sign-in risk policy to require MFA (or block) for medium and high-risk sign-ins. Configure user risk policy to require password change for high-risk users (leaked credentials detected). This automates response to threats detected by Microsoft's machine learning and threat intelligence.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Sign-in risks: anonymous IP, atypical travel, malware-linked IP, unfamiliar location.
  • User risks: leaked credentials, anomalous user activity.
  • Risk levels: low, medium, high; configure thresholds appropriately.
  • Self-remediation (password change) reduces admin burden.

questions.title: Service Principal Security
questions.scenario: Applications in your environment use service principals to access Azure resources. You need to secure these identities and detect compromised credentials.
questions.questionText: What security measures should you implement for service principals?

choices.text: Use managed identities where possible, certificate credentials for others, and workload identity federation for CI/CD
Client secrets with no expiration for stability
Shared service principal across all applications
Store credentials in application configuration files

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Consider the hierarchy of credential safety: no credentials at all, then hard-to-exfiltrate credentials, then avoidable secrets.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Prefer managed identities (system or user-assigned) which eliminate credential management entirely. For scenarios requiring service principals, use certificates over client secrets (harder to exfiltrate). For CI/CD, use workload identity federation to eliminate stored credentials. Monitor with Identity Protection for workload identities.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Managed identities: Azure manages credentials; auto-rotation; no exposure risk.
  • Certificate credentials: 1-2 year validity; rotation required; store in Key Vault.
  • Workload identity federation: OIDC tokens from GitHub/Azure DevOps exchanged for Azure tokens.
  • Monitor service principal sign-ins in Entra ID sign-in logs.

questions.title: Emergency Access Accounts
questions.scenario: You need to ensure access to Azure AD if Conditional Access is misconfigured or federated identity provider fails, while maintaining security of these emergency accounts.
questions.questionText: How should you configure emergency access (break-glass) accounts?

choices.text: Single account shared among all administrators
Federated accounts with the same IDP as regular users
Regular admin accounts with documented passwords
Cloud-only accounts, excluded from CA policies, FIDO2 keys, heavily monitored with alerts

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: What properties must an emergency account have so it still works when the very controls protecting normal accounts fail?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Create at least two cloud-only emergency access accounts (not federated). Exclude from all Conditional Access policies. Use FIDO2 security keys (phishing-resistant, no MFA fatigue). Store credentials securely (safe, separate locations). Monitor all sign-ins with immediate alerts. Test quarterly.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Cloud-only ensures access even if federation fails.
  • Different authentication methods per account (one FIDO2, one long password).
  • Global Administrator role permanently assigned (not eligible in PIM).
  • Alert on ANY sign-in; these accounts should rarely be used.

questions.title: Azure Firewall Configuration
questions.scenario: Your hub-spoke network requires centralized traffic inspection. You need to allow specific FQDNs for application updates, block known malicious IPs, and log all traffic.
questions.questionText: Which Azure Firewall features should you configure?

choices.text: Network rules only based on IP addresses
NAT rules for all outbound traffic
Application rules for FQDNs, threat intelligence filtering, and diagnostic logging to Log Analytics
Allow all traffic and rely on NSGs

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which firewall rule type lets you filter traffic by domain name rather than just IP, and what additional intelligence layer helps block known-bad destinations?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure Firewall application rules allow filtering by FQDN (e.g., *.microsoft.com) instead of IPs. Enable threat intelligence-based filtering to automatically block traffic to/from known malicious IPs. Configure diagnostic settings to send all logs to Log Analytics for security analysis and compliance.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Rule priority: NAT rules, Network rules, Application rules (in processing order).
  • FQDN tags: predefined groups like WindowsUpdate, AzureBackup.
  • Premium tier adds TLS inspection, IDPS, and URL filtering.
  • Forced tunneling requires management subnet for firewall health.

questions.title: DDoS Protection
questions.scenario: Your public-facing web application has been targeted by volumetric DDoS attacks. You need protection with attack analytics and cost protection during attacks.
questions.questionText: Which DDoS protection tier should you implement?

choices.text: DDoS Network Protection with diagnostic logging and cost protection

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Azure offers two DDoS tiers. Which one adds telemetry, adaptive tuning, and a cost guarantee beyond the basic always-on protection?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: DDoS Network Protection (formerly Standard) provides adaptive tuning based on your traffic patterns, real-time attack metrics and alerts, detailed attack analytics, and cost protection (credits for scale-out costs during attacks). Basic protection is automatic but lacks these advanced features.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Network Protection: per-VNet protection plan; ~$2,944/month base.
  • IP Protection: per-public-IP; cheaper for small deployments.
  • DDoS Rapid Response (DRR) team available during active attacks.
  • Combine with WAF for Layer 7 protection; DDoS handles Layer 3/4.

questions.title: Web Application Firewall
questions.scenario: Your web applications need protection against OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities, bot attacks, and custom threat patterns specific to your applications.
questions.questionText: How should you configure WAF for comprehensive protection?

choices.text: Allow all traffic and log for analysis
WAF policy with OWASP managed rules, bot protection, and custom rules in prevention mode
Custom rules only without managed rules

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about which combination layers industry-standard rulesets, automated bot detection, and app-specific filtering at the edge.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Enable OWASP managed rule sets (DRS 2.1 recommended) for comprehensive coverage of common vulnerabilities. Enable bot protection to block known malicious bots while allowing legitimate ones. Add custom rules for application-specific patterns. Run in prevention mode to actively block attacks.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Start in detection mode to tune false positives before prevention.
  • Exclusions allow bypassing rules for specific fields (e.g., file upload).
  • Per-site policies enable different rules for different applications.
  • WAF on Front Door provides global protection; App Gateway WAF is regional.

questions.title: Private Endpoint Security
questions.scenario: You're migrating PaaS services to use Private Endpoints. You need to ensure DNS resolution works correctly and that the public endpoints are disabled.
questions.questionText: What steps ensure secure Private Endpoint implementation?

choices.text: Keep public endpoints enabled as fallback
Use Service Endpoints instead for simplicity
Use Private Endpoints with public DNS resolution
Create Private DNS zones, link to VNets, disable public network access on services

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: How do you make a PaaS service's FQDN resolve to a private IP inside your VNet, and what must you disable to close the public path?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Create Azure Private DNS zones for each service type (e.g., privatelink.blob.core.windows.net). Link zones to VNets needing resolution. The Private Endpoint automatically registers in the zone. Disable public network access on the PaaS service to ensure all traffic uses the private path.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Centralize Private DNS zones in hub; link to all spoke VNets.
  • On-premises resolution requires DNS forwarder or Azure DNS Private Resolver.
  • NSG on Private Endpoint subnet controls access (requires enabling).
  • Disable public access: Storage firewall, SQL firewall, Key Vault firewall.

questions.title: Network Security Groups
questions.scenario: You need to allow web traffic to a subnet while blocking all other inbound traffic. Administrative access should only be allowed from a specific management subnet.
questions.questionText: How should you configure NSG rules?

choices.text: Allow HTTP/HTTPS from Internet, allow RDP/SSH from management subnet, deny all other inbound
Use only the default NSG rules
Block all traffic including required services
Allow all inbound traffic for flexibility

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Create explicit allow rules for required traffic; implicit deny blocks everything else.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: NSG rules are processed by priority (lower number = higher priority). Create allow rules for web ports (80, 443) from Internet. Create allow rules for management ports (3389, 22) from the management subnet only. The implicit DenyAllInbound rule at priority 65500 blocks all other traffic.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Application Security Groups (ASGs) simplify rules by grouping VMs logically.
  • NSG flow logs capture traffic decisions for analysis and compliance.
  • Associate NSGs with subnets (preferred) or individual NICs.
  • Augmented rules allow multiple ports/IPs in single rule (up to 4000 rules).

questions.title: Just-in-Time VM Access
questions.scenario: Your security team requires that management ports on VMs are closed by default and only opened temporarily when administrators need access.
questions.questionText: How should you implement this requirement?

choices.text: Use VPN for all management access
Keep management ports open with strong passwords
Enable JIT VM access in Microsoft Defender for Cloud
Manually modify NSG rules when access is needed

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which Defender for Cloud feature dynamically opens management ports only for an approved window, then locks them again?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Just-in-Time (JIT) VM access in Defender for Cloud blocks management ports by default via NSG rules. Administrators request access for a specific time window and source IP. Upon approval, JIT temporarily opens the port. Access automatically revokes when the time expires.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• JIT creates deny rules at priority 100; approval adds allow rules at priority 99.
  • Configure maximum request duration (e.g., 3 hours).
  • Requires Defender for Servers Plan 2 or Defender for Cloud (paid tier).
  • Combine with Azure Bastion for management without public IPs.

questions.title: Defender for Servers
questions.scenario: Your organization needs to protect VMs against malware, detect vulnerabilities, and monitor for suspicious activities indicating compromise.
questions.questionText: Which Defender for Servers capabilities address these requirements?

choices.text: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint integration, vulnerability assessment, and adaptive application controls

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about which Defender plan brings endpoint detection and response, vulnerability assessment, and application control to Azure VMs.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Defender for Servers includes Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (MDE) for real-time protection and EDR capabilities. Vulnerability assessment scans VMs for known CVEs. Adaptive application controls learn normal applications and alert/block unauthorized executables.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Plan 1: MDE integration only; Plan 2: adds vulnerability assessment, JIT, adaptive controls.
  • Qualys scanner included at no extra cost; Microsoft MDVM is alternative.
  • File integrity monitoring detects changes to sensitive files.
  • Agentless scanning available for supported VMs without agent installation.

questions.title: Container Security
questions.scenario: Your AKS clusters need protection against vulnerable images, runtime threats, and Kubernetes misconfigurations.
questions.questionText: Which Defender for Containers capabilities should you enable?

choices.text: Image scanning only without runtime protection
Image vulnerability scanning, runtime protection, and Kubernetes security posture

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Container security spans three layers: the images in the registry, the running workloads, and the cluster configuration. Which option addresses all three?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Defender for Containers scans images in Azure Container Registry for vulnerabilities. Runtime protection detects suspicious activities in running containers (cryptomining, reverse shells). Kubernetes security posture identifies misconfigurations against benchmarks (CIS, Azure baseline).

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Defender sensor (DaemonSet) collects runtime security data from nodes.
  • Azure Policy for Kubernetes enforces admission control (block vulnerable images).
  • Agentless scanning available for registries without Defender sensor.
  • CI/CD scanning with Defender extension for Azure DevOps/GitHub.

questions.title: App Service Security
questions.scenario: Your App Service hosts a customer-facing web application. You need to enforce HTTPS, restrict access to specific networks, and implement authentication.
questions.questionText: Which security configurations should you apply?

choices.text: HTTPS Only, VNet integration with access restrictions, Easy Auth with Entra ID

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Consider which combination enforces transport encryption, limits which networks can reach the app, and adds identity verification at the platform level.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Enable HTTPS Only to redirect all HTTP to HTTPS. Configure access restrictions to allow only specific IPs, VNets, or Service Endpoints. Use Easy Auth (Authentication/Authorization) to require Entra ID authentication without code changes. Enable managed identity for backend service access.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• TLS 1.2 minimum should be enforced; disable older versions.
  • Private Endpoints enable fully private App Service access.
  • Service Connector simplifies connecting to databases with managed identity.
  • App Service Environment (ASE) provides isolated, dedicated infrastructure.

questions.title: Azure Kubernetes Service Security
questions.scenario: Your AKS cluster needs to be hardened: API server should be private, pods should use managed identity for Azure access, and network policies should restrict pod-to-pod traffic.
questions.questionText: Which AKS security features should you configure?

choices.text: Public API server with IP restrictions only
Private cluster, Azure AD workload identity, and Calico/Azure network policies

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: What happens when the API server is not publicly reachable, pods authenticate without stored secrets, and east-west traffic is restricted?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Enable private cluster to make the API server accessible only via private endpoint. Use Azure AD workload identity (replacing pod identity) for pods to authenticate to Azure services without credentials. Enable network policy (Azure or Calico) to control pod-to-pod and pod-to-external traffic.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Private cluster requires Private DNS zone for API server resolution.
  • Workload identity uses federated tokens; no secrets stored in cluster.
  • Azure CNI vs Kubenet: CNI gives pods VNet IPs for direct network policy.
  • Defender profile integrates Defender for Containers protection.

questions.title: Storage Account Security
questions.scenario: Your storage accounts contain sensitive data. You need encryption with customer-managed keys, access only from your VNet, and immutable storage for compliance.
questions.questionText: Which storage security features should you configure?

choices.text: Service Endpoints with public access enabled
CMK encryption, Private Endpoints with disabled public access, immutable blob storage with legal hold

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about the three pillars: who controls the encryption keys, how the storage endpoint is reached, and whether stored data can be altered after write.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Enable customer-managed keys (CMK) in Key Vault for encryption key control. Use Private Endpoints for private network access and disable public network access entirely. Enable immutable blob storage with legal hold for data that cannot be modified or deleted during retention period.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Infrastructure encryption (double encryption) adds a second encryption layer.
  • Soft delete and versioning protect against accidental deletion.
  • Legal hold: indefinite immutability; time-based retention: configurable period.
  • Azure Policy can enforce these configurations across all storage accounts.

questions.title: Azure SQL Security
questions.scenario: Your Azure SQL Database contains PII. You need data encryption, row-level access control, sensitive data discovery, and threat detection.
questions.questionText: Which SQL security features should you implement?

choices.text: TDE with CMK, row-level security, data discovery and classification, Advanced Threat Protection

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Consider which option addresses encryption at rest, per-user data visibility, sensitive-data discovery, and threat detection in a single layered approach.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) with customer-managed keys encrypts data at rest. Row-level security (RLS) filters rows based on user context. Data discovery and classification identifies and labels sensitive columns. Advanced Threat Protection detects SQL injection, anomalous access, and data exfiltration.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Always Encrypted: client-side encryption; data never decrypted on server.
  • Dynamic data masking: masks data for non-privileged users.
  • Ledger: append-only, cryptographically verifiable tables.
  • Microsoft Purview extends classification to full data estate.

questions.title: Key Vault Security
questions.scenario: Your Key Vault stores cryptographic keys and secrets for production applications. You need to protect against accidental deletion, control access granularly, and audit all operations.
questions.questionText: Which Key Vault security features should you configure?

choices.text: Soft-delete with purge protection, RBAC access control, diagnostic logging to Log Analytics

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: How do you protect a Key Vault from accidental or malicious deletion, enforce least-privilege access, and maintain an audit trail?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Enable soft-delete (retains deleted items for 90 days) and purge protection (prevents purging during retention). Use RBAC for granular access control (e.g., Key Vault Secrets User for reading secrets only). Configure diagnostic settings to send audit logs to Log Analytics for security monitoring.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Soft-delete enabled by default; purge protection must be explicitly enabled.
  • RBAC vs access policies: RBAC is recommended; supports individual secret permissions.
  • Private Endpoints eliminate public network exposure.
  • HSM-backed keys provide FIPS 140-2 Level 3 protection.

questions.title: Data Loss Prevention
questions.scenario: You need to prevent sensitive data (credit card numbers, SSNs) from being stored in unauthorized locations or shared externally.
questions.questionText: Which solution provides data loss prevention capabilities?

choices.text: Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention policies

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which service can detect sensitive data types across Microsoft 365 and automatically block or restrict unauthorized sharing?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies identify sensitive information types (credit cards, SSNs, custom patterns) and enforce actions: block sharing, require justification, notify admins. DLP covers Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, and endpoint devices.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Sensitive information types: 300+ built-in; custom types for organization-specific data.
  • DLP policies can apply to specific users, groups, or locations.
  • Endpoint DLP extends protection to Windows/macOS devices.
  • Sensitivity labels integrate with DLP for classification-based policies.

questions.title: Cosmos DB Security
questions.scenario: Your globally distributed Cosmos DB contains customer data. You need network isolation, encryption with customer-managed keys, and fine-grained access control.
questions.questionText: How should you secure the Cosmos DB account?

choices.text: Private Endpoints, CMK encryption, Azure AD RBAC for data plane operations
Primary key shared across all applications

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about three layers: network isolation for the data plane, customer-controlled encryption, and identity-based authorization instead of shared keys.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Use Private Endpoints to eliminate public network exposure. Enable customer-managed keys for encryption control. Configure Azure AD RBAC for data plane access, allowing identity-based permissions instead of sharing primary keys. This eliminates credential management while enabling fine-grained access.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Data plane RBAC roles: Cosmos DB Data Reader, Data Contributor, etc.
  • Disable key-based authentication after migrating to RBAC.
  • Always Encrypted: client-side encryption for highly sensitive fields.
  • Disable local auth: disallows primary/secondary key authentication.

questions.title: Microsoft Sentinel Deployment
questions.scenario: You need to implement a cloud-native SIEM for threat detection, investigation, and automated response across your Azure environment and on-premises systems.
questions.questionText: How should you deploy Microsoft Sentinel?

choices.text: Sentinel workspace with data connectors, analytics rules, and playbooks for automation
Log Analytics workspace without Sentinel features

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which option combines log ingestion, correlation-based detection, and automated response into a single cloud-native SIEM/SOAR platform?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Enable Microsoft Sentinel on a Log Analytics workspace. Configure data connectors to ingest logs from Azure services, Microsoft 365, on-premises, and third-party sources. Enable analytics rules to detect threats. Create playbooks (Logic Apps) for automated investigation and response.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Content hub provides packaged solutions with connectors, rules, and workbooks.
  • UEBA (User and Entity Behavior Analytics) detects anomalous behavior.
  • Fusion uses ML to correlate low-fidelity alerts into high-confidence incidents.
  • Cost: pay per GB ingested; commitment tiers provide discounts.

questions.title: Security Alerts and Incidents
questions.scenario: Your SOC receives hundreds of security alerts daily. You need to prioritize critical threats, reduce alert fatigue, and streamline incident investigation.
questions.questionText: How should you manage security alerts in Defender for Cloud and Sentinel?

choices.text: Alert suppression rules for known benign, incident correlation, and automated triage playbooks

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: How do you reduce noise from known-benign alerts, group related signals together, and speed up the first response steps?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Create suppression rules for alerts that are known benign (e.g., authorized security scanning). Sentinel automatically correlates related alerts into incidents for unified investigation. Build playbooks to automate initial triage: enrich alerts with threat intelligence, run queries, and escalate critical incidents.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Alert severity: High, Medium, Low, Informational; prioritize by severity.
  • MITRE ATT&CK mapping helps understand attack tactics and techniques.
  • Automation rules trigger playbooks automatically on incident creation.
  • Watchlists enrich alerts with organizational context (VIP users, critical assets).

questions.title: Threat Hunting
questions.scenario: Your security team needs to proactively search for threats that may have evaded automated detection, using hypothesis-driven queries.
questions.questionText: How should you enable threat hunting in your environment?

choices.text: Wait for alerts to indicate threats
Sentinel hunting queries with KQL, bookmarks, and livestream for real-time hunting

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Proactive threat hunting needs a query language, a way to save interesting findings, and a way to watch results live. Which toolset offers all three?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Microsoft Sentinel provides built-in and custom hunting queries using KQL. Hunters develop hypotheses and query logs for indicators. Bookmarks save interesting results for investigation. Livestream allows real-time query execution during active incidents. Promote successful hunts to analytics rules.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Hunting queries can be scheduled as analytics rules after validation.
  • Notebooks (Jupyter) enable advanced analysis with Python libraries.
  • MITRE ATT&CK coverage shows gaps in detection for specific techniques.
  • TI (Threat Intelligence) integration enriches hunting with IOCs.

questions.title: Secure Score
questions.scenario: Management wants visibility into your organization's security posture and a prioritized list of actions to improve security.
questions.questionText: Which feature provides security posture assessment with recommendations?

choices.text: Microsoft Defender for Cloud Secure Score

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which Defender for Cloud feature gives you a single numeric measure of your security posture with prioritized improvement actions?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Defender for Cloud Secure Score aggregates security findings into a percentage score. Recommendations are prioritized by potential impact on the score. Each recommendation includes remediation steps and often a Quick Fix option. Track score over time to demonstrate security improvement.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Secure Score covers multiple security domains: identity, data, compute, network.
  • Exemptions allow accepting risk for specific recommendations.
  • Regulatory compliance shows adherence to standards (CIS, NIST, PCI-DSS).
  • Score impacts from recommendations help prioritize high-value fixes.

questions.title: Compliance Management
questions.scenario: Your organization must demonstrate compliance with HIPAA, PCI-DSS, and SOC 2. You need continuous compliance monitoring and evidence collection.
questions.questionText: How should you manage compliance in Azure?

choices.text: Defender for Cloud regulatory compliance dashboard with Azure Policy initiatives

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about which tool maps your security controls to regulatory frameworks and pairs with a governance engine for continuous enforcement.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Defender for Cloud regulatory compliance dashboard shows continuous compliance status against standards (HIPAA, PCI-DSS, SOC 2, NIST). Azure Policy initiatives define required controls and report non-compliance. Export compliance reports for auditors. Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager provides additional compliance tools.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Add additional regulatory standards from the compliance dashboard.
  • Custom compliance standards can be created using Azure Policy.
  • Continuous export sends compliance data to Log Analytics or Event Hub.
  • Service Trust Portal provides Microsoft audit reports and compliance documentation.

questions.title: Cross-Tenant Access
questions.scenario: Your organization collaborates with partner companies. You need to control which external organizations can access your resources and what access your users have to external organizations.
questions.questionText: How should you configure cross-tenant access?

choices.text: Cross-tenant access settings with inbound and outbound policies per organization
Allow all B2B collaboration without restrictions

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: When you need per-organization control over inbound and outbound B2B collaboration, where in Entra ID do you configure those policies?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Entra ID cross-tenant access settings define inbound policies (what external users can do in your tenant) and outbound policies (what your users can do in external tenants). Configure default settings for all organizations and override for specific trusted partners with more permissive access.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• B2B collaboration: guest users in your tenant.
  • B2B direct connect: shared channels without guest accounts (Teams).
  • Trust settings: trust partner MFA and device claims to reduce friction.
  • Organizational relationships: specify tenant IDs for trusted partners.

questions.title: Azure RBAC Best Practices
questions.scenario: Your organization is assigning Azure permissions. You need to follow the principle of least privilege while maintaining operational efficiency.
questions.questionText: Which RBAC practices should you implement?

choices.text: Create custom roles for every user
Assign Owner at subscription level for simplicity
Use built-in roles at narrowest scope, assign to groups, use PIM for privileged roles

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Consider three RBAC best practices: minimizing the scope of each assignment, simplifying who holds the role, and limiting how long the access lasts.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Assign roles at the narrowest appropriate scope (resource group > subscription > management group). Use built-in roles before creating custom ones. Assign to Entra ID groups for easier management. Use PIM for privileged roles to reduce standing access. Regular access reviews ensure ongoing appropriateness.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Scope hierarchy: permissions inherit from parent to child.
  • Deny assignments exist but are rare; managed by Azure Blueprints.
  • Classic roles (Service Administrator, Co-Administrator) are legacy; migrate to RBAC.
  • Custom roles can be scoped to specific subscriptions or management groups.

questions.title: Network Segmentation
questions.scenario: Your workloads have different security requirements: public-facing web tier, application tier, and sensitive data tier. You need to isolate these tiers.
questions.questionText: How should you design network segmentation?

choices.text: Separate subnets with NSGs, Azure Firewall for inter-tier traffic, and Private Endpoints for data tier

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: A three-tier architecture needs segmentation between tiers, deep traffic inspection between them, and private-only access to the data layer. Which combination achieves this?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Create separate subnets for each tier with NSGs restricting traffic to required ports and sources. Route inter-tier traffic through Azure Firewall for inspection and logging. Use Private Endpoints for data tier access, eliminating public network exposure. This creates defense in depth.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Microsegmentation: NSGs and ASGs for fine-grained pod-to-pod rules.
  • Azure Firewall Premium: TLS inspection for encrypted traffic visibility.
  • Subnet delegation: some services require dedicated subnets.
  • Service tags simplify NSG rules for Azure services.

questions.title: VM Disk Encryption
questions.scenario: Your VMs contain sensitive data. You need to encrypt OS and data disks with customer-managed keys and ensure encryption at the host level.
questions.questionText: Which encryption options should you configure?

choices.text: Azure Disk Encryption or Encryption at Host with customer-managed keys in Key Vault

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about where disk encryption can be applied: inside the guest OS versus at the hypervisor layer. Which option gives you customer-managed key control at either level?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure Disk Encryption (ADE) uses BitLocker (Windows) or DM-Crypt (Linux) for OS and data disk encryption. Encryption at Host provides encryption before data leaves the VM, including temp disks and caches. Both support customer-managed keys stored in Key Vault for key control.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• ADE vs Encryption at Host: ADE is guest-level; EaH is platform-level.
  • Server-side encryption (SSE) is always on for managed disks (at rest).
  • Double encryption: SSE + ADE or SSE + EaH for compliance requirements.
  • Confidential VMs: use AMD SEV-SNP for memory encryption.

questions.title: Azure Backup Security
questions.scenario: Ransomware attacks target backups to prevent recovery. You need to protect backup data from deletion or encryption by attackers.
questions.questionText: Which Azure Backup security features should you enable?

choices.text: Backups without soft delete for immediate cleanup
Soft delete, immutable vaults, multi-user authorization, and enhanced security

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: How do you protect backup data from both accidental deletion and insider threats that could destroy or modify recovery points?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Enable soft delete to retain deleted backup data for 14 additional days. Configure immutable vaults to prevent deletion or early expiration of backups. Multi-user authorization (MUA) requires Resource Guard approval for critical operations. Enhanced security provides additional malware scanning and alerts.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Soft delete: 14-day retention; can be extended; cannot be disabled once enabled.
  • Immutability: locked policies prevent even admins from deleting backups.
  • Resource Guard: separate resource in different subscription for MUA.
  • Private Endpoints for backup traffic; restrict access to Recovery Services vault.

questions.title: Security Automation
questions.scenario: Your security team wants to automate responses to common security incidents: isolating compromised VMs, blocking malicious IPs, and notifying stakeholders.
questions.questionText: How should you implement security automation?

choices.text: Sentinel playbooks with Logic Apps for automated response actions

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which SOAR mechanism in Azure lets you define automated investigation and response workflows triggered by security incidents?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Microsoft Sentinel playbooks are Logic Apps triggered by alerts or incidents. They can automatically isolate VMs (NSG changes), block IPs in firewall, enrich alerts with threat intelligence, create tickets in ServiceNow, and notify via Teams/email. Automation rules control when playbooks run.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Playbook triggers: alert trigger (per alert) or incident trigger (correlated).
  • Built-in playbook templates for common scenarios (isolate VM, block IP).
  • Managed identity or service principal for playbook to take actions.
  • Test playbooks in non-production before enabling automated execution.

questions.title: Passwordless Authentication
questions.scenario: Your organization wants to eliminate passwords to reduce phishing risk and improve user experience.
questions.questionText: Which passwordless authentication methods should you deploy?

choices.text: Windows Hello for Business, FIDO2 security keys, and Microsoft Authenticator passwordless

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which authentication approach eliminates the password entirely, making credential phishing and replay attacks impossible?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Deploy Windows Hello for Business for managed Windows devices (biometric or PIN backed by TPM). Offer FIDO2 security keys for shared devices or users preferring hardware tokens. Enable Microsoft Authenticator passwordless for mobile users. All three are phishing-resistant unlike password+SMS.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• FIDO2: open standard; works across platforms; no shared secrets.
  • Windows Hello: device-bound credential; biometric or PIN; TPM protected.
  • Certificate-based authentication (CBA): another phishing-resistant option.
  • Authentication strength in Conditional Access can require phishing-resistant methods.

questions.title: Azure Bastion
questions.scenario: Administrators need secure access to VMs without exposing management ports to the internet or requiring VPN clients.
questions.questionText: How should you configure Azure Bastion for secure VM access?

choices.text: Bastion Standard tier with native client support, shareable links disabled, and diagnostics enabled
Public IPs on all VMs with NSG restrictions
Jump box VM with public IP

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: How can you provide RDP/SSH access to VMs without exposing public IPs, and which tier adds native client and link-sharing capabilities?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure Bastion provides secure RDP/SSH through the Azure portal without public IPs on VMs. Standard tier enables native client (az network bastion tunnel), file upload/download, and host scaling. Disable shareable links in production for security. Enable diagnostic logs for audit.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Bastion requires dedicated subnet named AzureBastionSubnet (/26 minimum).
  • Premium tier: session recording, private-only deployment.
  • Can be shared across peered VNets to reduce cost.
  • Combine with JIT access for additional protection on management ports.

questions.title: Confidential Computing
questions.scenario: Your application processes highly sensitive data. You need to protect data while in use, ensuring even Azure operators cannot access it.
questions.questionText: Which Azure service provides hardware-based data-in-use protection?

choices.text: Azure Confidential VMs with AMD SEV-SNP or Intel TDX

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: What technology protects data while it is actively being processed in memory, even from the cloud provider's infrastructure?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure Confidential VMs use AMD SEV-SNP or Intel TDX to create hardware-based Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs). Memory is encrypted with keys inaccessible to Azure. Remote attestation verifies the environment before releasing sensitive data. This protects data even from privileged administrators.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Full memory encryption: entire VM memory encrypted, not just enclaves.
  • Attestation: cryptographic proof of TEE integrity before processing.
  • Confidential containers: AKS confidential computing nodes.
  • Always Encrypted with secure enclaves: SQL Server data processing in TEE.

questions.title: Microsoft Purview Data Governance
questions.scenario: Your organization needs visibility into sensitive data across Azure, on-premises, and multi-cloud environments for governance and compliance.
questions.questionText: Which solution provides unified data discovery and classification?

choices.text: Azure Resource Graph for data discovery
Microsoft Purview Data Map with automated scanning and sensitivity labels

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which service automatically discovers, classifies, and catalogs sensitive data across your multi-cloud estate?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Microsoft Purview Data Map scans data sources (Azure, AWS, on-premises) to discover and classify data automatically. It identifies sensitive information types (PII, PCI, PHI) and applies sensitivity labels. Data catalog provides lineage, glossary, and governance insights across the data estate.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Scans: Azure Blob, ADLS, SQL, Cosmos DB, Synapse, AWS S3, on-premises SQL.
  • Classification rules: built-in for 200+ types; custom patterns supported.
  • Data lineage: visualize data flow from source to destination.
  • Integration with Defender for Cloud for security insights.

questions.title: Log Analytics Security
questions.scenario: Your Log Analytics workspace contains sensitive security logs. You need to control who can query specific tables and protect log integrity.
questions.questionText: How should you secure the Log Analytics workspace?

choices.text: Table-level RBAC, resource-context access, and customer-managed keys
No access controls for operational efficiency
Public access to logs for transparency

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: How do you restrict which Log Analytics tables a user can query, limit visibility to only their own resources, and keep the data encrypted under your own key?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Configure table-level RBAC to grant access to specific tables only (e.g., security team to SecurityEvent). Enable resource-context access mode so users only see logs from resources they have access to. Use customer-managed keys for encryption control. Enable data export for long-term retention in secure storage.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Access modes: workspace-context (see all data in workspace) vs resource-context (see data for accessible resources).
  • Custom log tables can have different RBAC than built-in tables.
  • Dedicated cluster: isolated compute, CMK, and commitment tier pricing.
  • Search job: query archived data from long-term storage.

questions.title: Entitlement Management
questions.scenario: External contractors need time-limited access to Azure resources and applications. Access should be self-service with approval workflows and automatic expiration.
questions.questionText: How should you manage external user access lifecycle?

choices.text: Manual guest user creation without expiration
Entra ID Entitlement Management with access packages, approval workflows, and automatic expiration

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which Entra ID feature lets users request bundled access to resources through a governed, self-service workflow with automatic expiration?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Entra ID Entitlement Management creates access packages bundling group memberships, app access, and SharePoint sites. External users request access via portal; workflows route to approvers. Access automatically expires after configured period. Access reviews ensure ongoing necessity.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Connected organizations: configure for known partner companies.
  • Multiple policies per package: different rules for internal vs external.
  • Separation of duties: requestor cannot be sole approver.
  • Lifecycle workflows: automate onboarding/offboarding tasks.

questions.title: ExpressRoute Security
questions.scenario: Your ExpressRoute connection provides private connectivity to Azure. You need to ensure traffic is encrypted and that the connection meets security requirements.
questions.questionText: How should you secure ExpressRoute traffic?

choices.text: Configure MACsec for ExpressRoute Direct or IPsec VPN over ExpressRoute
No additional encryption needed for private connection

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: ExpressRoute traffic is private but not encrypted by default. What Layer 2 or Layer 3 encryption options can you add to protect data in transit?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: ExpressRoute provides private connectivity but doesn't encrypt traffic by default. For ExpressRoute Direct, enable MACsec for point-to-point encryption between your router and Microsoft's. Alternatively, create a VPN tunnel over ExpressRoute for IPsec encryption. This addresses compliance requirements for encryption.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• MACsec: Layer 2 encryption; requires ExpressRoute Direct (dedicated ports).
  • IPsec over ExpressRoute: create VPN Gateway and connect via ExpressRoute path.
  • Application-level TLS is always recommended regardless of network encryption.
  • ExpressRoute Global Reach traffic between on-premises sites is not encrypted.

questions.title: Update Management
questions.scenario: Your VMs need regular security patches. You need to assess missing updates, schedule maintenance windows, and report compliance.
questions.questionText: How should you manage VM updates?

choices.text: Azure Update Manager with assessment, scheduled deployments, and compliance reporting
Defer all updates until annual maintenance

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which Azure service gives you a single pane for assessing missing patches, scheduling deployments, and reporting compliance across VMs?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure Update Manager assesses VMs for missing updates, schedules update deployments during maintenance windows, and reports compliance status. Configure pre/post scripts for graceful application handling. Supports Windows and Linux VMs in Azure, on-premises, and other clouds via Arc.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Update classifications: Critical, Security, Definition, Update Rollup, etc.
  • Maintenance configurations define when updates can be applied.
  • Azure Policy can audit or enforce update compliance.
  • Hotpatch (preview) applies updates without reboot for supported Windows.

questions.title: Threat Intelligence
questions.scenario: Your security team needs to enrich alerts with threat intelligence and proactively hunt for known indicators of compromise (IOCs).
questions.questionText: How should you integrate threat intelligence?

choices.text: Manual IOC lookup for each alert
Rely on vendor threat feeds only
Microsoft Sentinel Threat Intelligence with TI connectors and TI-based analytics rules

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: How can you ingest external threat intelligence feeds and automatically match indicators of compromise against your collected logs?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Microsoft Sentinel Threat Intelligence imports indicators from Microsoft Defender TI, TAXII feeds, and custom sources. TI-based analytics rules automatically match indicators against logs to detect known threats. TI workbench helps analyze and manage indicators for hunting.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Indicator types: IP, domain, URL, file hash, email address.
  • Microsoft Defender Threat Intelligence (MDTI) provides premium TI.
  • STIX/TAXII: standard formats for threat intelligence sharing.
  • TI matching rules: correlate indicators with network, DNS, and file logs.

questions.title: Sensitivity Labels
questions.scenario: Your organization needs to classify and protect documents based on sensitivity level. Protection should persist when documents are shared externally.
questions.questionText: How should you implement document classification and protection?

choices.text: Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels with encryption and rights management

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which mechanism embeds classification and persistent encryption directly into a document so protection follows the file wherever it goes?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels classify and protect documents and emails. Labels can apply encryption (Azure Rights Management), content markings (headers, watermarks), and access restrictions. Protection persists when documents are shared externally. Auto-labeling can apply labels based on content.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Label hierarchy: Public < General < Confidential < Highly Confidential.
  • Encryption options: user-defined permissions or admin-defined protection.
  • Auto-labeling: client-side recommendations or service-side automatic application.
  • Double Key Encryption (DKE) for highest sensitivity with customer-held key.

questions.title: Access Reviews
questions.scenario: You need to periodically verify that users still need their access to groups, applications, and Azure roles.
questions.questionText: How should you implement ongoing access validation?

choices.text: Entra ID Access Reviews with regular schedules and automatic removal

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: What Entra ID feature periodically asks reviewers to confirm whether users still need their access, and can auto-revoke if they don't respond?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Entra ID Access Reviews create periodic reviews for group memberships, application access, and Azure roles. Reviewers (managers, self, or designated) confirm or deny access. Configure automatic actions: remove denied access, remove if not reviewed, or notify only. Supports PIM role assignments.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Review frequency: weekly, monthly, quarterly, annually.
  • Multi-stage reviews: multiple reviewers in sequence.
  • Decision helpers: show recommendations based on last sign-in.
  • Access review history for compliance audit trails.

questions.title: Network Watcher Security
questions.scenario: You need to troubleshoot network connectivity issues, verify NSG rules are working correctly, and capture traffic for security analysis.
questions.questionText: Which Network Watcher features should you use?

choices.text: IP flow verify for NSG testing, connection troubleshoot, and packet capture for analysis

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which Azure networking toolkit lets you test whether NSG rules allow or deny a specific flow, diagnose connectivity issues, and capture packets?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: IP flow verify tests whether traffic is allowed/denied by NSG rules. Connection troubleshoot diagnoses connectivity issues between Azure resources. Packet capture collects network traffic for deep analysis. NSG flow logs show all traffic decisions for security monitoring and compliance.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• IP flow verify: shows which NSG rule allowed/denied specific traffic.
  • NSG flow logs: JSON logs of all NSG decisions; sent to storage or Log Analytics.
  • Traffic Analytics: visualizes NSG flow logs with insights on traffic patterns.
  • Connection Monitor: continuous connectivity testing and alerting.

questions.title: Function App Security
questions.scenario: Your Azure Functions process sensitive data. You need to secure the function app, protect secrets, and control network access.
questions.questionText: Which security configurations should you apply?

choices.text: VNet integration, Key Vault references for secrets, managed identity, and function access keys

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Consider how to isolate a serverless function's outbound traffic, protect its secrets without hardcoding, authenticate to resources without credentials, and restrict who can invoke it.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Enable VNet integration to access private resources and optionally restrict inbound access. Use Key Vault references in app settings instead of storing secrets directly. Enable managed identity for authenticating to Azure services. Configure function-level access keys (function/admin) or Easy Auth for human access.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Authorization levels: Anonymous, Function, Admin.
  • Private Endpoints: fully private function app access.
  • Deployment slots: separate keys, useful for blue-green deployments.
  • IP restrictions: limit inbound to specific networks or services.

questions.title: Security Benchmarks
questions.scenario: Your organization needs to align Azure configurations with industry security standards and best practices.
questions.questionText: Which framework provides Azure-specific security best practices?

choices.text: Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark (MCSB) implemented via Defender for Cloud
Custom security standards without industry alignment

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which Azure-native security benchmark maps controls to industry frameworks, and what service continuously assesses your compliance against it?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark (MCSB) provides Azure-specific security controls covering network, identity, data protection, and more. Controls map to CIS, NIST, and PCI-DSS. Defender for Cloud's default initiative assesses against MCSB and provides recommendations for remediation.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• MCSB v3: organized by security functions (Network, Identity, Data, etc.).
  • Control domains: Network Security, Identity Management, Privileged Access, Data Protection, etc.
  • Azure Security Benchmark is predecessor; MCSB is multi-cloud.
  • CIS Azure Benchmarks provide additional hardening guidance.

questions.title: Token Protection
questions.scenario: Attackers have stolen access tokens and are using them from different devices. You need to prevent stolen token replay attacks.
questions.questionText: Which feature prevents stolen token replay?

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: What Conditional Access capability prevents a stolen session token from being replayed on a different device?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Conditional Access token protection (sign-in session token binding) cryptographically binds access tokens to the device's TPM. If an attacker steals the token and tries to use it from a different device, the token validation fails. This mitigates token theft attacks like pass-the-token.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Token protection requires Windows 10/11 with TPM and supported apps.
  • Currently in preview; initially supports desktop Office apps.
  • Continuous Access Evaluation (CAE) enables near real-time policy enforcement.
  • Complements sign-in frequency and persistent browser controls.

questions.title: Storage Access Tiers
questions.scenario: You need to securely archive audit logs for 7 years while minimizing storage costs and maintaining data protection.
questions.questionText: How should you configure storage for long-term retention?

choices.text: Archive tier with immutability policy and access tiering automation

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: For long-term regulatory retention, think about which storage tier minimizes cost, what prevents data modification, and how tiering can be automated.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Store long-term audit logs in Archive tier (~$0.002/GB/month). Apply time-based immutability policy to prevent modification or deletion for 7 years. Use lifecycle management rules to automatically move logs from Hot to Cool to Archive based on age. Retrieval requires rehydration.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Archive tier: lowest cost; up to 15 hours for standard retrieval.
  • Immutability: WORM (Write Once, Read Many) for compliance.
  • Legal hold: indefinite immutability for litigation preservation.
  • Soft delete protects against accidental deletion during retention period.

questions.title: Workbook Security Monitoring
questions.scenario: Your security team needs custom dashboards to visualize security data: identity risks, network threats, and compliance status.
questions.questionText: How should you create security visualizations?

choices.text: Azure Workbooks with KQL queries against Sentinel and Defender data
Export data to Excel for manual charting

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Which Azure visualization tool lets you build interactive, KQL-driven dashboards from Log Analytics and security data?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Azure Workbooks provide interactive reports and dashboards using KQL queries. Query data from Log Analytics, Sentinel, and Defender for Cloud. Combine visualizations (charts, grids, maps), parameters for filtering, and drill-down capabilities. Share workbooks across the team or organization.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Sentinel content hub includes pre-built workbooks for many data sources.
  • Parameters enable interactive filtering without editing queries.
  • Groups organize visualizations with tabs or accordions.
  • Export to PDF or share via workbook templates.

questions.title: DNS Security
questions.scenario: You need to protect against DNS-based attacks and ensure DNS queries from your VNets are logged and monitored.
questions.questionText: How should you secure DNS in your Azure environment?

choices.text: Azure Firewall DNS proxy with DNS logging and threat intelligence filtering

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: How can you gain visibility into DNS queries leaving your VNet, block resolutions to known-malicious domains, and log every lookup?

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Enable Azure Firewall DNS proxy to intercept all DNS queries from VNets. Configure custom DNS servers pointing to Azure Firewall. Threat intelligence filtering blocks queries to known malicious domains. DNS logs in Log Analytics enable monitoring for DNS tunneling or C2 communication.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Azure Firewall Premium: FQDN filtering in network rules requires DNS proxy.
  • DNS logs show queried domains, source IPs, and resolutions.
  • DNS threat intelligence: blocks domains flagged as malicious.
  • Azure DNS Private Resolver provides hybrid DNS without custom VMs.

questions.title: Security Governance at Scale
questions.scenario: Your enterprise Azure environment spans multiple subscriptions. You need to enforce security policies consistently and report on compliance across the entire estate.
questions.questionText: How should you implement security governance at scale?

choices.text: Management groups with Azure Policy initiatives, Defender for Cloud coverage, and centralized Sentinel

hints.label: Brief Hint
hints.content: Think about which hierarchy lets you govern policies across all subscriptions, what provides posture assessment, and what centralizes security operations.

hints.label: Complete Explanation
hints.content: Organize subscriptions under management groups and assign Azure Policy security initiatives at the management group level for consistent enforcement. Enable Defender for Cloud across all subscriptions for unified security posture management. Centralize security logs in a single Sentinel workspace for unified threat detection and response.

hints.label: Deep Knowledge
hints.content:
• Azure Landing Zone architecture provides governance foundation.
  • Lighthouse enables MSP-style cross-tenant management.
  • Continuous export sends Defender alerts to Sentinel automatically.
  • Policy exemptions should be time-limited and tracked.

gl-zero-trust.name: Zero Trust
gl-zero-trust.definition: Security model that assumes breach and verifies each request as though it originates from an untrusted network, enforcing least-privilege access.
gl-zero-trust.examNote: Key principles: verify explicitly, use least-privilege access, assume breach.

gl-conditional-access.name: Conditional Access
gl-conditional-access.definition: Entra ID feature that enforces access policies based on conditions like user risk, device state, location, and application.
gl-conditional-access.examNote: Creates if-then policies; enables zero trust for identity.

gl-pim.name: Privileged Identity Management
gl-pim.definition: Azure AD service providing just-in-time privileged access with activation workflows, time limits, and audit trails.
gl-pim.examNote: Reduces standing privileged access; requires Entra ID P2.

gl-defender-cloud.name: Microsoft Defender for Cloud
gl-defender-cloud.definition: Cloud security posture management (CSPM) and workload protection platform (CWPP) providing security recommendations and threat protection.
gl-defender-cloud.examNote: Secure Score measures posture; Defender plans protect specific workloads.

gl-sentinel.name: Microsoft Sentinel
gl-sentinel.definition: Cloud-native SIEM and SOAR solution for threat detection, investigation, and automated response.
gl-sentinel.examNote: Built on Log Analytics; uses KQL for queries; playbooks automate response.

gl-cmk.name: Customer-Managed Keys
gl-cmk.definition: Encryption keys stored in customer's Key Vault, providing control over encryption key lifecycle for Azure services.
gl-cmk.examNote: Enables key rotation, revocation, and compliance with key management requirements.

gl-private-endpoint.name: Private Endpoint
gl-private-endpoint.definition: Network interface providing private IP access to PaaS services, eliminating public network exposure.
gl-private-endpoint.examNote: Requires Private DNS zones for name resolution; disable public access on services.

gl-jit.name: Just-in-Time VM Access
gl-jit.definition: Defender for Cloud feature that blocks management ports by default and opens them temporarily upon approved request.
gl-jit.examNote: Reduces attack surface; creates deny rules at priority 100.
